newsitem.title: INDIA: India receives 184,098 tonnes Australian wheat.
newsitem.headline: India receives 184,098 tonnes Australian wheat.

text.p: A total of 184,098 tonnes of imported Australian wheat carried on five vessels has arrived in five Indian ports, India's Commerce Ministry said on Wednesday.
The ships are berthed at Vizag, New Mangalore, Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT), Kakinada and Karwar ports, it said in a statement.
The ministry said another 14 ships carrying 487,000 tonnes of wheat set out from Australia for India on February 3.
The transport wing of India's state-run State Trading Corporation (STC), Transchart, had contracted 27 vessels for the import of 932,000 tonnes of wheat from Australia, the statement said.
Two more ships for the import of another 60,000 tonnes of wheat from Australia are likely to be contracted shortly, it said.
Transchart has contracted seven vessels with a total capacity of 237,000 tonnes for wheat from Canada, the statement said.
"The imports are targetted to be completed by the end of March," it said.
In December, the federal government authorised the import of up to two million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April-March) to increase supplies and check rising domestic prices.
Last month STC said it had bought 1.25 million tonnes of wheat. STC has tendered for another 50,000 tonnes. The results are expected in the next few days.
The state-run Food Corporation of India has arranged for the discharge of wheat from the ports to various distribution centres, the statement said.
So far 34,000 tonnes of the imported wheat have already been dispatched for distribution, it said.
